title: Incident groups, group mappings (properties, operations, rule order, default group) and priorities

prose.text: {{group-access}} {{group-delete-order}} The groups an incident is assigned and how its priority follows from them are in [[zwa.incidents]].

prose.label: Operations and predicates.
prose.text: {{operations-by-type}} {{operation-semantics}} {{predicate-functions}} {{predicate-limit}} What NOT, EXISTS and LIKE do beyond that is open {{gap:operation-details}}.

group-access.statement: Admins with Full or Restricted access to Workflow Automation can add incident groups, but only admins with Full access can map them.

quotes: Admins with Full or Restricted access to Workflow Automation can add incident groups, but only admins with Full access to Workflow Automation can map those incident groups.

group-delete-order.statement: A mapped incident group can be deleted only after its incident group mappings have been deleted.

quotes: If the incident group is mapped, the incident group mappings must be deleted first before you can delete the incident group.

priority-values.statement: An incident group can be assigned a priority of critical, high, medium or low, and incident groups must be added before priorities are managed.

quotes: They can assign a priority of critical, high, medium, or low to an incident group.
Before managing priorities for incident groups, add incident groups on the Incident Group page of the Zscaler Admin Console.

priority-change-group.statement: On the Priorities page, changing the incident group on a priority row removes the priority from the previous incident group and adds it to the new one.

quotes: If you change the incident group, the priority is removed from the previous incident group and added to the new incident group.

mapping-source-type.statement: The Source DLP type choices for an incident group mapping are Any, Email, Endpoint, Inline and SaaS Security; Any appears by default.

quotes: Source DLP types are Any, Email, Endpoint, Inline, and SaaS Security. Any appears by default.
evidence.after: To configure a basic incident mapping:

predicate-limit.statement: A mapping statement can hold up to 100 predicates.

quotes: You can add up to 100 predicates for a statement.
evidence.after: Add a predicate for the first condition:

property-types.statement: All attributes in an incident transaction are available as mapping properties; the selectable properties vary with the Source DLP type chosen, and a property can be a number, string, date or Boolean.

quotes: All the attributes in an incident transaction are available as properties.
The properties available for selection vary depending on the Source DLP type you select.
A property can be a number, a string, a date, or a Boolean field (True or False).

mapping-obfuscation.statement: User attributes chosen for obfuscation cannot be used as mapping properties, and a user with obfuscation enabled cannot edit existing mappings that were created using an obfuscation field.

quotes: If you choose user attributes for obfuscation, you cannot map an incident group to these obfuscated attributes (properties).

if a user with permissions to incident group mappings has obfuscation enabled and an incident group was previously mapped using an obfuscation field, then the user cannot edit those existing incident group mappings.

csv-only-properties.statement: Several User Info mapping properties exist only when CSV is selected as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page: Home Country, Job Title, Location, Organization Hierarchy, Phone Number, Project IDs, Termination Date, User Role, Worker Type, and the Skip Level Managers properties.

quotes: Home Country (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
Job Title (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
Location (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
Organization Hierarchy (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
Phone Number (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
Project IDs (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
Termination Date (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
User Role (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
Worker Type (only available if you select CSV as the primary user data source on the Account Settings page)
The Skip Level Managers properties are only available if you select CSV as your primary user data source on the Account Settings page.

source-scoped-properties.statement: Mapping properties with a stated Source DLP type scope: Client IP and Protocol are available only for Inline; Device Name, Device OS, Device Trust Level and the Endpoint Info properties only for Endpoint; the Application Info properties only for Inline, SaaS Security and Email; Severity is not available for Email.

quotes: Client IP (only available for Source DLP type Inline)
Protocol (only available for Source DLP type Inline)
Device Name (only available for Source DLP type Endpoint)
Device OS (only available for Source DLP type Endpoint)
Device Trust Level (only available for Source DLP type Endpoint)
The Endpoint Info properties are available only for Source DLP type Endpoint.
The Application Info properties are available only for Source DLP types of Inline, SaaS Security, and Email.
Severity (not available for Source DLP type Email)

operations-by-type.statement: Mapping operations are tied to property types: AFTER and BEFORE to Date; CONTAINS_EXACT and NOT_CONTAINS_EXACT to Array of strings, Number and Boolean; EQUALS and NOT_EQUALS to String, Number and Date; IN_IPv4_SUBNET and IN_IPv6_SUBNET to IP Address; LIKE to String; LESS_THAN and GREATER_THAN to Number; EXISTS to all types.

quotes: AFTER It can be used for a Date type property field.
BEFORE It can be used for a Date type property field.
| CONTAINS_EXACT It can be used for the following types of property fields: Array of strings Number Boolean
NOT_CONTAINS_EXACT It can be used for the following types of property fields: Array of strings Number Boolean
| EQUALS It can be used for the following types of property fields: String Number Date
NOT_EQUALS It can be used for the following types of property fields: String Number Date
IN_IPv4_SUBNET It can be used for an IP Address type property field.
IN_IPv6_SUBNET It can be used for an IP Address type property field.
LIKE It can be used for a String type property field.
LESS_THAN It can be used for a Number type property field.
GREATER_THAN It can be used for a Number type property field.
EXISTS It can be used for all types of property fields.

operation-semantics.statement: LIKE does a partial substring comparison; EXISTS takes no property value; the CONTAINS example maps incidents that violated several rules including Block-HIPAA-SSN to one group using matchingPolicies.rules[*].name with CONTAINS_EXACT.

quotes: This operation does a partial comparison of the substring.
For this type of operation, you do not enter a property value.

Using the CONTAINS operation, you can ensure that those incidents with multiple rule violations that include the Block-HIPAA-SSN rule are mapped to the Social Security Number Violations incident group.
Property = matchingPolicies.rules[*].name Operation = CONTAINS_EXACT Property Value = Block-HIPAA-SSN (must contain the full name of the DLP rule)

predicate-functions.statement: A new predicate row is added with the AND function selected; OR or AND can be chosen when another predicate is added, and NOT can be selected.

quotes: Another predicate row appears under the first predicate row, and the AND function is automatically selected for the condition.
You can only select OR or AND as the function when you add another predicate.
Functions are NOT, OR, and AND.

rule-processing.statement: Rules equate to statements; all rules are processed for an incident transaction, so a transaction matching several rules can be assigned to multiple incident groups, and the order of rules is set with the up and down arrows.

quotes: Rules equate to statements in Workflow Automation.

Workflow Automation processes through all the rules for an incident transaction. If a transaction matches a rule, the incident group associated with the rule is assigned to the transaction. Depending on your rules, a transaction might be assigned to multiple incident groups.
click the down arrow or up arrow next to an incident group to arrange the order in which the rules are processed.

default-group.statement: When no other incident group mapping matches an incident, Workflow Automation uses the default incident group.

quotes: When Workflow Automation finds no other matches for any other incident group mapping for an incident, it uses the default incident group for the incident.

mapping-access.statement: Only admins with full access to Workflow Automation can map incident groups, and incident groups are then assigned to restricted-access admins on the Admin Assignment page.

quotes: Only admins with full access to Workflow Automation can map the incident groups.
After incident groups are configured, admins with full access can then assign these incident groups to the admins with restricted access who will be responsible for them.
They do these assignments in the Zscaler Admin Console, on the Admin Assignment page.

operation-details.title: What NOT does to an operation, how EXISTS treats an empty array, and whether LIKE is case sensitive
operation-details.detail: The operations table gives the property types each operation accepts and says only EQUALS, NOT_EQUALS, CONTAINS_EXACT and NOT_CONTAINS_EXACT are not case sensitive; it does not state the effect of the NOT function on an operation, EXISTS on an empty array, or LIKE case sensitivity.
